verdict: Block's gross profit rose 25% to $3.2B — Cash App up 31%, Square up 13% — but a steep tax bill and an $88M paper loss on its bitcoin holdings cut reported net income to $89M.

kpis.label: Gross profit
kpis.note: +25% YoY — the number Block steers by

kpis.label: Square GPV
kpis.note: +12% YoY; U.S. growth strongest since Q2 2023

segments.name: Commerce enablement
segments.note: Square's business: payment processing and tools for sellers, plus Cash App's commerce features. Square's gross payment volume was $74,734M, up 12% — U.S. volume growth was the strongest since Q2 2023.

segments.name: Financial solutions
segments.note: Cash App's money products — Borrow loans, Afterpay buy-now-pay-later, the Cash App Card and banking features. Almost all of this revenue is kept: costs were just $94M against $1,382M of revenue.

segments.name: Bitcoin ecosystem
segments.note: Bitcoin bought and sold through Cash App, plus Block's bitcoin hardware and mining efforts. Enormous revenue, almost no profit: $1,821M of costs against $1,894M of revenue left just $72M of gross profit.

flow.costPlain: What Block pays to run each transaction and product: card-network fees for sellers, the cost of Cash App's money features, and the bitcoin Block buys to resell — $1,821M of the total is bitcoin cost alone.

opex.name: Product development
opex.note: Engineers and designers building Square, Cash App and Block's bitcoin products.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Winning sellers for Square and new users for Cash App.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal, people and offices.

opex.name: Transaction & loan losses
opex.note: Money Block expects not to collect on Cash App Borrow, Afterpay and seller loans — the cost of being a lender.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of companies Block has bought.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net $56M, an $88M non-cash loss from revaluing Block's bitcoin holdings and $1M of other expense came to $145M; the $1M loss borne by noncontrolling interests brings the net hit to common shareholders to $144M.
footerNote: Net income is the figure attributable to common stockholders.
pngFooterNote: Net income shown is attributable to common stockholders.
follow100Note: Bitcoin is the illusion in Block's revenue: $28.62 of every $100 comes in from bitcoin sales and $27.53 goes straight back out to buy the bitcoin. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Gross profit is the growth story
takeaways.text: Gross profit rose 25% to $3,166M — Cash App contributed $1,974M (+31%) and Square $1,157M (+13%). Block raised its full-year gross profit guidance to $12.51B.

takeaways.title: Record adjusted profitability
takeaways.text: Adjusted operating income hit a record $864M — a 27% margin on gross profit — and adjusted EPS rose 65% to $1.02. Block's own AI tools are part of the story: in June, agentic AI helped write and review nearly all of its production code changes.

takeaways.title: Tax and bitcoin hid the progress
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS fell to $0.15 from $0.87 a year ago. An $88M paper loss on bitcoin (a $212M gain a year ago) and a $214M tax provision on $301M of pre-tax income — a 71% effective rate — did the damage, not the operating business.

oneTimers: An $88M non-cash loss from revaluing Block's bitcoin holdings — versus a $212M gain in the same quarter last year — sits below operating income and is the biggest single reason net income fell to $89M from $538M.
The $214M tax provision on $301M of pre-tax income is a 71% effective rate, far above Block's usual level — taxes, not operations, squeezed this quarter's bottom line.
Adjusted figures strip out share-based compensation and other items: adjusted operating income was $864M versus $447M GAAP, and adjusted EPS $1.02 versus $0.15 GAAP.
